newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton settles weaker in light volume.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton settles weaker in light volume.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed barely weaker in most-active July amid thin and rangebound dealings, floor sources said.

A dearth of news kept prices within a narrow range after this morning's spec/hedge report failed to inspire movement. The report showed the speculators to be holding a 19.3 percent net short position, little changed from last week's data.
July ended 0.08 cent weaker at 73.45 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.55 to 72.95 cents. New-crop December finished down 0.09 at 75.87 cents.
Volume was estimated at 6,000 lots compared with Monday's official 4,031 lots.
Delayed plantings and talk that growers are switching to other crops, failed to inspire gains as business remains slow, market sources said. Players await Thursday's export and sales report.
Certificated stocks as of April 28 were unchanged from the previous session at 220,870 480-lb bales.
Open interest in May stood at only 350 lots, down 253 lots as of early Monday. Interest in July fell by 199 lots to 41,490 lots.
A total of 600 notices have been issued to date.
